NoteNlpAccessor::metaphone¶

Back to Note NLP Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note NoteNlpAccessor::metaphone() const

Reduce Each Word To Its Consonant Skeleton¶

metaphone() replaces each cell with a compact pronunciation key for every word it contains: the first letter, then the remaining consonants with vowels and near-silent letters removed. programming → PRGRMNG. It keeps more of a word’s shape than the four-character soundex code, so it is a better fuzzy-match key for longer words.

The key¶

Each word is upper-cased and reduced as follows:

  1. Keep the first letter.

  2. From the rest, drop every vowel (A E I O U), every H, W, and Y, and every non-letter.

  3. Drop a consonant that immediately repeats the previous kept letter.

  4. Truncate to at most eight characters.

This is a lightweight consonant-skeleton key. It is not the full Metaphone algorithm: it does not apply letter-context rules such as PH to F, CK to K, or silent GN, so Pfister keeps both P and F as PFSTR. A separate double-Metaphone operation is not exposed because the implementation does not produce the alternate key that would make that contract meaningfully different.

Per cell¶

The cell is tokenized into words (letters and digits; punctuation is a separator), each word is reduced, and the keys are joined with a single space. A cell with no word yields an empty string.

The operation is shape-preserving and cell-independent, works on UTF-8 text (a bytes-mode Note is rejected with NoteNlpAccessor::metaphone requires a UTF-8 text Note (not bytes)), and returns a fresh UTF-8 Note. Non-ASCII letters are not decoded — run to_ascii first if the input has accents.

Example 1: Names¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({"Thompson", "knight", "programming", "Pfister"})
        .nlp().metaphone())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[4], dim=1, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
["TMPSN", "KNGT", "PRGRMNG", "PFSTR"]

Thompson keeps T then MPSN (the H and both Os drop); knight keeps K then NGT (I drops, and this key does not silence the K or GH).

Example 2: Multi-Word Cells¶

std::cout << pluss::make_note({"quick brown fox"}).nlp().metaphone() << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["QCK BRN FX"]

See Also¶

  • NoteNlpAccessor::soundex: a fixed four-character “sounds-like” code.

  • NoteNlpAccessor::to_ascii: fold accents to ASCII before coding.

  • NoteNlpAccessor::tokens: the word split used per cell.
